back: Ores — a natural resource that will eventually run out.
Heat then slowly cool the metal — removes stress, makes it softer and refines its structure.
Heat then cool at room temperature — reduces hardness and increases ductility.
Heat then rapidly cool (quench) in water or oil — increases hardness but makes steel brittle.
Hardened steel is cleaned, reheated to a lower temperature (judged by oxide colour, straw to blue) and quenched — reduces brittleness and increases toughness while keeping most of the hardness.

front: Why can't mild steel be hardened and tempered?
back: It does not contain enough carbon.
Adding carbon to the surface, then heating and quenching — gives a hard surface with a tough core.
Kiln drying or air drying to remove moisture and prevent shrinkage.
Recycled wooden waste mixed with adhesive, e.g. MDF, chipboard, hardboard, plywood.
Thermoplastics (thermoforming) can be heated and shaped repeatedly; thermosets can only be heated and shaped once.
Acrylic, polythene, polypropylene, polystyrene, nylon and Styrofoam.
Melamine formaldehyde, urea formaldehyde and epoxy resin.

front: How paper and card are measured
back: Paper by weight in gsm; card (board) by thickness in microns.
